inspiration.observed_pattern: A MySQL/MariaDB migration drops an existing named foreign-key constraint and re-adds the same constraint with a revised delete action.
inspiration.mysql_mariadb_translation: Reauthored as a parcel manifest migration. An existing restrictive parcel-item foreign key is dropped and recreated with ON DELETE SET NULL; deleting one parcel then nulls only its item references while preserving the items. The source schema, names, values, and issue-tracking purpose are new.

fixture_notes: Parcel 5001 owns two items and parcel 5002 owns one. The original RESTRICT action would block deletion; after replacement with SET NULL, deleting 5001 leaves its items with NULL parcel IDs and preserves parcel 5002's relationship.
determinism_notes: All parcel and item IDs are fixed and final reads use primary-key ordering. No clocks, randomness, sleeps, or concurrent connections are used.
setup: CREATE TABLE parcels (parcel_id INT PRIMARY KEY, route_code VARCHAR(16) NOT NULL)

CREATE TABLE parcel_items (item_id INT PRIMARY KEY, parcel_id INT NULL, item_code VARCHAR(16) NOT NULL, CONSTRAINT fk_parcel_items_parcel FOREIGN KEY (parcel_id) REFERENCES parcels (parcel_id) ON DELETE RESTRICT)

steps.sql: ALTER TABLE parcel_items DROP FOREIGN KEY fk_parcel_items_parcel
ALTER TABLE parcel_items ADD CONSTRAINT fk_parcel_items_parcel FOREIGN KEY (parcel_id) REFERENCES parcels (parcel_id) ON DELETE SET NULL

checks.sql: SELECT parcel_id, route_code FROM parcels ORDER BY parcel_id
SELECT item_id, parcel_id, item_code FROM parcel_items ORDER BY item_id
